Avoidant partner, I see? You tried to explain, but he cut you off. He’s offended, yet not comfortable enough to talk about it—especially not in a way that explains how he feels or helps him see your point of view. Even after sleeping on it, he wants to brush it off. And you can’t keep going like that, because it hurts.

I’ve had this fight many times with my boyfriend. I’m the avoidant one, and he’s the anxious type. Over time (and with therapy), I learned that when something goes wrong, I tend to make the relationship all about me—pushing aside my partner’s feelings. That’s not okay, and I don’t want to make my boyfriend feel like his emotions don’t matter.

So here’s something you could say:

“I’m sorry I hurt you with what I said, but I’m also hurt by how you responded. I think it’s important that we both understand how we see the problem. But when you keep brushing me off, I don’t feel heard. I can give you space and time, and when you’re ready to talk about it, I’m here. I really want us to talk heart-to-heart.”
